script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The passage says the king will reign in righteousness; it does not say whether he will reign in silence.
The joke mentions milk, a food not permitted here. It also gives the cookie milk, making the comparison hard to follow.
The rulers are compared to streams and a rock in dry land. The passage does not say they literally show up where things are parched.
The verse says a fool will no longer be called noble and a scoundrel will not be respected. It does not say all titles will match the people holding them.
Saying neither person will get honored anymore goes beyond the specific things the verse says about the fool and scoundrel.
The passage says the fool leaves the hungry empty and deprives the thirsty of drink. It does not say he walks past them.
The verse says the noble man stands up for worthy causes; it does not give his reason or method for picking them.
A harvest failing is not necessarily the opposite of fruit ripening. The verse says the harvest will fail, not that the grapes will not ripen.
The passage describes the land as overgrown and the city as abandoned, but does not say the land itself is lost.
The passage calls the hill and watchtower a delight for wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks. It does not say wild donkeys are the only ones enjoying the city.
The verse names the wilderness and the fertile field. 'Nothing is left out' extends its statement beyond those places.
The verse says the work of righteousness will be peace; it does not say righteousness requires less physical effort or sweat than expected.
